Act as the implementation sub-agent for this task.

You are implementing ONE issue in the Email OS Vue/Tauri client (repo = your worktree). Read first: PRODUCT.md, DESIGN.md (type scale, Mono token, reader notes, standing constraint "message content renders as safe literal plain text"), src/components/ReaderView.vue, src/assets/style.css (:root tokens near top, .message-body, .reader-scroll).

## Shared rules (all reader-review tasks)
- Context: we compared our conversation reader against a Superhuman screenshot. Superhuman message bodies are proportional sans, generous line height (~1.6-1.7), measure ~90 characters, wide comfortable reading. Ours: monospace 13.6px (`--type-mono` 0.85rem) full-width 944px column ≈ 110 chars/line, which reads like code.
- Stay on-brand per PRODUCT.md/DESIGN.md: terse, honest-state, keyboard-first, no AI/sparkle features. Message content must stay text-interpolated only (no v-html, no markdown/HTML processing, whitespace preserved with pre-wrap).
- Keep every existing `data-test` attribute, aria-label and keyboard behaviour; update tests in tests/ and src that your change legitimately affects (e.g. rendered-layout gates referencing mono). Do NOT edit DESIGN.md or PRODUCT.md — put design-doc notes (the token changes, rationale) in your final report.
- Other agents are changing the same files in parallel on separate branches (toolbar→header, collapsed snippets, Details/focus-ring dedupe, star status line, active-card style, recent-mail filter). Keep your diff MINIMAL and localized (ideally just tokens + the .message-body / .messages rules); no reformatting.
- Setup: `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`. Verify with `pnpm typecheck` and `pnpm test` (full suite; report honestly incl. pre-existing failures).
- Preview: `pnpm dev --port <PORT> --strictPort` (in-memory fixture workspace). Use mcp__t3-code__preview_* tools (load via ToolSearch), resize 1280x800, press Enter on the focused first row to open "Fixture thread 1: weekly status". Stop dev server and close preview tab when done.
- Evidence: save PNGs under the evidence dir below (mkdir -p). BEFORE (base commit) and AFTER at 1280x800 via preview_snapshot save=true (copy screenshotPath to named files). If blurry, retry and add getBoundingClientRect/computed-style measurements in the report.
- Commit on your worktree's branch (no push, no PR). End the commit message with: `Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`.
- Final report (brief): branch + head SHA, files changed, what you did, tests run/results, evidence absolute paths, DESIGN.md notes, anything you couldn't do.

## Your issue: P2 – Body type and measure
- Cap the message body measure to about 80-90ch (use `max-width: 80ch`-style on `.message-body`, measured in the body font), left-aligned with the message header; the surrounding list/rules/cards still span the column.
- Switch message body from mono to the proportional UI face (system-ui, matching --font) at a reading size larger than the 12px shell body: choose a token (e.g. `--type-reading`, ~0.9375rem–1rem) with line-height ~1.55-1.65, keeping `white-space: pre-wrap` and `overflow-wrap:anywhere`. Hard-wrapped plain-text emails (quoted lines starting with ">" , signature blocks, ASCII tables, code) lose alignment in a proportional face: handle this honestly — keep a way to see the raw monospace text. Simplest acceptable: add a per-reader toggle (keyboard shortcut wired through App.vue's single keyboard dispatcher + a palette command in src/lib/action-palette.ts if the repo's patterns make that easy; otherwise a small quiet "Monospace" button in the message Details area) — OR keep mono automatically for messages whose body has lines starting with ">" / 2+ consecutive lines with 4+ leading spaces / table-ish pipes. Pick whichever is smallest and most predictable, and explain the choice in the report. Default for normal prose = proportional.
- Do not change the `--type-mono` token value used by other surfaces (check usages with grep; drafts editor etc.).
- Verify with a multi-paragraph body, and a body with a quoted block (temporarily tweak the fixture in a scratch edit, screenshot, and revert the fixture).
